<USER_REQUEST>
So I want you to check something.  In our installer I think we are pushing some of our hooks outside the pluginto get them working - I think we may have hacked it up.   Here is the definitive info on plugins for hooks etc:

Plugin hooks.json Discovery & Enablement in Antigravity
1. Where hooks.json Lives in a Plugin
Per the bundled customizations documentation (~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md), a plugin's lifecycle hooks live directly at the plugin root alongside plugin.json:

~/.gemini/config/plugins/repo-memory/
├── plugin.json       # Required manifest
├── hooks.json        # Lifecycle hooks (PreInvocation, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, etc.)
├── mcp_config.json   # Optional MCP servers
└── sidecars/         # Optional sidecars

When a plugin is enabled, its hooks.json is automatically merged with workspace (.agents/hooks.json) and global (~/.gemini/hooks.json) hooks, with relative command paths resolved against the plugin directory. When a plugin is disabled, it still appears in the plugin inventory, but none of its bundled customizations (hooks.json, mcp_config.json, rules/, skills/) are loaded.


2. Why repo-memory Hooks Don't Fire Out of the Box (While datacloud_telemetry and .agents/hooks.json Do)
As documented in ~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md and ~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/plugin/SKILL.md:

Workspace .agents/hooks.json is not a plugin: Standalone hooks.json files are loaded directly without a plugin enablement gate.
Plugins with sidecar permission grants start disabled until approved/enabled:
A simple plugin that only ships plugin.json and hooks.json (like googlecloudtools.datacloud_telemetry) requires no permission setup and starts enabled by default.
Empirically, when a plugin bundles a sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json that declares agent_permissions (such as access_grants or workspace_uris) or MCP server variables, Antigravity treats the plugin as requiring setup/permission review and defaults it to disabled ("disabled": true) until the user explicitly enables it.
Central enablement state in ~/.gemini/config/config.json persists across reinstalls:
Antigravity records plugin enablement in ~/.gemini/config/config.json under plugins.<dir_name>.enabled (keyed by the directory name repo-memory, not the name field inside plugin.json).
As noted in plugin/SKILL.md (Step 2A), config.json always takes precedence over the plugin directory itself and persists across reinstalls. If "repo-memory": { "enabled": false } was written to config.json when the plugin was first discovered in a disabled state, re-running repo-memory install will not enable it unless config.json (or the language server state) is updated.


3. How to Verify & Enable the Plugin
Option A: Via the agy CLI (Recommended)
Run:

agy plugin enable repo-memory

You can verify that the plugin's hooks are now active by running /hooks inside an Antigravity session (which lists active hooks from enabled plugins as of v1.2.3).
Option B: Inspect & Enable Live via the Language Server RPC (plugin/SKILL.md)
From an Antigravity terminal where ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS and ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN are set, you can inspect the live plugin state using the inventory command from ~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/plugin/SKILL.md:

# 1. Check whether repo-memory is discovered, whether hooksJson is loaded, and whether disabled is true:
curl -sS -X POST \
  "http://${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS}/exa.language_server_pb.LanguageServerService/GetAllPlugins" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-codeium-csrf-token: ${ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}' | jq '[.plugins[] | select(.path | endswith("/repo-memory")) | {
    name,
    dir: (.path | split("/") | last),
    disabled: (.disabled // false),
    hooksLoaded: ((.hooksJson // "") | length > 0)
  }]'

# 2. Enable repo-memory live (no restart required if the directory was already discovered on startup):
curl -sS -X POST \
  "http://${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS}/exa.language_server_pb.LanguageServerService/JetboxWriteState" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-codeium-csrf-token: ${ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"userConfig":{"plugins":{"repo-memory":{"enabled":true}}}}'

(Note per plugin/SKILL.md Step 4: if ~/.gemini/config/plugins/repo-memory/ was created for the very first time while Antigravity was already running, a one-time restart is needed for initial plugin directory discovery; subsequent enable/disable toggles take effect live.)


4. Recommended Fixes for repo-memory install --harness antigravity
To make repo-memory fire hooks out of the box after installation:

Remove agent_permissions from packaging/antigravity/sidecar.json: Because sidecars/tick/sidecar.json uses "builtin": "schedule" to run the repo-memory tick binary directly as an OS subprocess rather than an agent session requesting tool permissions, agent_permissions.access_grants is unnecessary. Omitting agent_permissions allows the plugin to default to enabled on fresh installs (matching googlecloudtools.datacloud_telemetry).
Ensure plugins.repo-memory.enabled is set to true on install: Have repo-memory install --harness antigravity either run agy plugin enable repo-memory or ensure "plugins": { "repo-memory": { "enabled": true } } is set in ~/.gemini/config/config.json (and cleaned up on uninstall) so a prior "enabled": false entry does not keep the plugin disabled across reinstalls.

</USER_REQUEST>

7: Autonomous bug fixer loop plugin for Google Antigravity (AGY). It provides a 3-loop background agent system that autonomously triages, fixes, tests, and opens pull requests for small bugs and TODOs in a target repository while human engineers focus on major feature work and architectural PRs.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## Overview
12: 
13: Modern software development often suffers from an accumulation of small bugs, DX papercuts, and un-ignored test cases that distract maintainers from core product development. `bug-fixer-loop` operates as a trusted, guard-railed junior engineer:
14: 
15: - **Runs in background sidecars** on bounded cron schedules.
16: - **Respects human maintainer PR priority** via an active-PR exclusion zone.
17: - **Guarantees security & boundary defense** through PreToolUse hooks, safe ingestion filters, and mandatory test passes.
18: - **Never auto-merges**: All changes are delivered as clean, atomic Pull Requests for human review.
19:

9: # Antigravity Customization System Guide
10: 
11: The Antigravity Customization System allows you to tailor the agent's behavior,
12: teach it new workflows, enforce guidelines, and integrate it with external
13: tools. By customizing the agent, you can transition it from a general-purpose
14: assistant to an expert pair programmer specialized in your project's codebase

21: Choose the right customization type based on your goal:

23: Type            | Config File/Folder           | Scope                     | Best For                                                                                | Learn More

28: **Hooks**       | `hooks.json`                 | Lifecycle Event           | Running scripts/commands at specific agent lifecycle points (e.g., pre-tool execution). | [Hooks Guide](./docs/hooks.md)

33: ## Customization Discovery and Locations
34: 
35: Antigravity automatically discovers your own customizations by traversing
36: specific directories. Built-in customizations are not found this way: the agent
37: config names the ones it mounts.
38: 
39: ### Discovery Locations
40: 
41: 1.  **Workspace Customizations** (Project-Specific):
42:     *   Path: `.agents/` (or `.agent/`, `_agents/`, `_agent/`) at the root of
43:         your project.
44:     *   Use this to share customizations with your team by checking them into
45:         version control (VCS).
46:     *   The agent walks from your current working directory up to the repository
47:         root (e.g., the folder containing `.git`) to find these directories.
48: 2.  **Directory & Project Rules** (Hierarchical):
49:     *   Paths: `GEMINI.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/*.md`
50:     *   As you open or edit files, the agent walks up from the file's directory
51:         to the repository root, loading all rules it finds.
52: 3.  **Global Configuration** (Machine-Local):
53:     *   Path: `~/.gemini/config/`
54:     *   Applies to all projects and workspaces run on your machine.
55: 
56: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
57: 
58: ## Loading Priority and Precedence
59: 
60: When multiple customizations are discovered, they are loaded and applied in a
61: specific order. If there are naming conflicts (e.g., two skills with the same
62: name), the higher-priority customization overrides the lower-priority one.
63: 
64: The priority order (from highest to lowest) is:
65: 
66: 1.  **Workspace Project**: Hierarchical discovery walking up from the CWD to the
67:     repository root.
68: 2.  **Declared Configurations**: Customizations explicitly listed in
69:     `skills.json` or `plugins.json` in your workspace.
70: 3.  **Global Discovery**: `~/.gemini/config/`
71: 4.  **Built-in Customizations**: Default skills bundled with the application,
72:     mounted by name rather than discovered.
73: 5.  **Global Declared Configurations**: Explicitly listed in global JSON
74:     configs.
75: 
76: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
77: 
78: ## How Customizations are Applied
79: 
80: ### Progressive Disclosure (Skills and Rules)
81: 
82: To prevent overwhelming the model's context window, Antigravity uses
83: **progressive disclosure**:
84: 
85: *   **Skills** are not loaded into the context window by default. Only their
86:     names and descriptions are injected. The full content of a skill is only
87:     loaded if the model (or the user) explicitly decides to activate it.
88: *   **Rules** with `trigger: model_decision` behave similarly. Only `always_on`
89:     rules are loaded unconditionally.
90: 
91: ### Deduplication
92: 
93: All customizations (especially rules) are deduplicated by their resolved file
94: paths. A rule file will never be injected more than once in a single
95: conversation turn, even if it matches multiple trigger conditions.

103: configurations.

3: Plugins are namespaced, shareable bundles that package **Skills**, **Rules**,

10: ## Directory Structure
11: 
12: A plugin must be contained within a subdirectory of a `plugins/` folder in a
13: customization root (e.g., `.agents/plugins/`).
14: 
15: ```text
16: plugins/<plugin_name>/
17: ├── plugin.json       # Required: Manifest file
18: ├── mcp_config.json   # Optional: MCP servers exposed by the plugin
19: ├── hooks.json        # Optional: Lifecycle hooks run by the plugin
20: ├── rules/            # Optional: Rules applied when plugin is active (AGENTS.md recommended)
21: │   └── AGENTS.md
22: └── skills/           # Optional: Skills exposed by the plugin
23:     └── <skill_name>/
24:         └── SKILL.md
25: ```
26: 
27: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
28: 
29: ## Manifest (`plugin.json`)
30: 
31: The `plugin.json` file serves as the marker declaring the directory as a plugin.
32: 
33: ```json
34: {
35:   "name": "team-developer-kit"
36: }
37: ```
38: 
39: *   **`name`** (string, optional): The display name of the plugin. If omitted,
40:     it defaults to the directory name.
41: 
42: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
43: 
44: ## How Plugins Work
45: 
46: When a plugin is discovered and enabled:
47: 
48: 1.  **Automatic Ingestion**: All skills, rules, hooks, and MCP servers defined
49:     within the plugin's directory structure are automatically loaded.
50: 2.  **Namespacing**: Tools and skills exposed by the plugin are namespaced if
51:     necessary to prevent collisions with other customizations.
52: 3.  **Lifecycle Scoping**:
53:     *   **Hooks** defined in `plugins/<name>/hooks.json` are registered and run
54:         during the agent's lifecycle.
55:     *   **MCP Servers** defined in `plugins/<name>/mcp_config.json` are
56:         launched, and their tools are made available.
57:     *   **Rules** in `plugins/<name>/rules/` are merged into the active rule
58:         set. Placing a consolidated **`AGENTS.md`** (or `GEMINI.md`) file under
59:         `rules/` (e.g., `rules/AGENTS.md`) is recommended over separate rule files.
60: 
61: ## Registering Plugins
62: 
63: Plugins can be discovered automatically if placed in standard customization
64: roots, or they can be explicitly registered using `plugins.json`.
65: 
66: *   See the [JSON Configurations Guide](./json_configs.md) for details on how to
67:     use `plugins.json` to enable specific plugins or inherit them from shared
68:     paths.
69: 
70: ## Turning Plugins On and Off
71: 
72: Most discovered plugins are **enabled by default**; a plugin can ship switched
73: off by declaring `"disabled": true` in its `plugin.json`, and some built-in ones
74: do. Whether a plugin is active is recorded in your `config.json`, under a
75: `plugins` map keyed by the plugin's **directory** name:
76: 
77: ```json
78: {
79:   "plugins": {
80:     "my-plugin": { "enabled": false }
81:   }
82: }
83: ```
84: 
85: You can change the setting from the plugin section of the settings UI, or from
86: the CLI's `plugin enable` / `plugin disable` subcommands, both of which write
87: this entry.
88: 
89: `config.json` wins wherever it has an entry, so your choice always beats what

91: declaration, which is how a plugin that ships disabled stays off until you turn

93: your choice survives reinstalling or updating the plugin.
94: 
95: A disabled plugin still appears in the plugin list so you can turn it back on,

1: # JSON Configuration Files
2: 
3: JSON configuration files allow you to explicitly register and manage
4: customizations that are stored outside the default discovery locations (such as
5: project-specific folders or shared team directories).
6: 
7: Each customization type has its own configuration file, placed in your
8: customization root directory (e.g., `.agents/` in your project, or
9: `~/.gemini/config/` globally):
10: 
11: *   **Skills**: `skills.json`
12: *   **Plugins**: `plugins.json`
13: 
14: ## Configuration Schema
15: 
16: Both configuration files share the same schema, allowing you to declare path
17: entries and inherit from other configurations.
18: 
19: ```json
20: {
21:   "inherits": [
22:     {
23:       "path": "/path/to/shared/skills.json",
24:       "include_only": ["linter-skill"],
25:       "exclude": ["deprecated-skill"]
26:     }
27:   ],
28:   "entries": [
29:     {
30:       "path": "path/to/my/project/skills",
31:       "exclude": ["experimental-.*"]
32:     },
33:     {
34:       "path": "~/personal-skills"
35:     }
36:   ]
37: }
38: ```
39: 
40: ### Top-Level Fields
41: 
42: *   **`entries`** (array of objects, optional): A list of path entries to scan
43:     for customizations of this type. Each entry directory is scanned **one level
44:     deep**.
45: *   **`inherits`** (array of objects, optional): A list of other configuration
46:     files to inherit from. The entries from inherited files are merged with your
47:     local entries. Inherited files are processed in the order they are listed.
48: 
49: ### Path Entry Fields
50: 
51: Each object in the `entries` or `inherits` array supports the following fields:
52: 
53: | Field          | Type             | Required | Description                   |
54: | :------------- | :--------------- | :------- | :---------------------------- |
55: | `path`         | string           | Yes      | The path to the customization |
56: :                :                  :          : directory (for `entries`) or  :
57: :                :                  :          : another JSON config file (for :
58: :                :                  :          : `inherits`).                  :
59: | `include_only` | array of strings | No       | Patterns naming items         |
60: :                :                  :          : relative to `path`. If        :
61: :                :                  :          : specified, only matching      :
62: :                :                  :          : customizations will be        :
63: :                :                  :          : loaded.                       :
64: | `exclude`      | array of strings | No       | Patterns. Customizations      |
65: :                :                  :          : whose directory names match   :
66: :                :                  :          : any of these patterns will be :
67: :                :                  :          : skipped.                      :
68: 
69: ## Explicitly Configured Paths
70: 
71: Config files are also honored on explicitly configured customization paths (e.g.
72: `skills_paths` in an agent's customization discovery config) when the configured
73: path points directly at a config file (e.g. `path/to/skills.json`). A configured
74: directory keeps its regular one-level scan; a manifest inside it is not
75: expanded. Directories referenced from manifest `entries` follow the standard
76: one-level entry scan, and top-level `exclude` patterns apply across all
77: explicitly configured paths, not just the one that declared them. They never
78: filter customizations inherited from the user's environment.
79: 
80: ## Path Resolution Rules
81:

# Antigravity Plugin Hooks — Complete Reference > How hooks are discovered, loaded, gated by plugin enablement, and what must be true for them to fire. --- ## Table of Contents 1. [Two Hook Systems: Standalone vs Plugin-Bundled](#1-two-hook-systems) 2. [Hook Discovery Locations](#2-hook-discovery-locations) 3. [The Plugin Enablement Gate](#3-the-plugin-enablement-gate) 4. [What Blocks Plugin Hooks](#4-what-blocks-plugin-hooks) 5. [How to Enable/Disable a Plugin](#5-how-to-enabledisable-a-plugin) 6. [Plugin Directory Structure](#6-plugin-directory-structure) 7. [hooks.json File Format](#7-hooksjson-file-format) 8. [Hook Input/Output Contracts](#8-hook-inputoutput-contracts) 9. [Path Resolution in Plugin Hooks](#9-path-resolution-in-plugin-hooks) 10. [Diagnostic Flowchart](#10-diagnostic-flowchart) 11. [Bug Fixer Loop — Current State vs Correct Approach](#11-bug-fixer-loop-analysis) --- ## 1. Two Hook Systems There are **two fundamentally different ways** hooks can be loaded, and they behave very differently: ### A. Standalone Hooks (Always Loaded) A `hooks.json` file placed directly in a customization root directory: | Location | Scope | Gated by plugin enablement? | |----------|-------|-----------------------------| | `/.agents/hooks.json` | Workspace (project-specific) | ❌ **No** — always loaded | | `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` | Global (all projects) | ❌ **No** — always loaded | These hooks fire **unconditionally** whenever the workspace or global config is active. There is no enable/disable gate. The only way to stop them is to delete or rename the file, or set `"enabled": false` on individual hook entries within the file. ### B. Plugin-Bundled Hooks (Gated by Plugin Enablement) A `hooks.json` file placed **inside a plugin directory**, next to `plugin.json`: | Location | Scope | Gated by plugin enablement? | |----------|-------|-----------------------------| | `/.agents/plugins//hooks.json` | Workspace plugin | ✅ **Yes** | | `~/.gemini/config/plugins//hooks.json` | Global plugin | ✅ **Yes** | These hooks **only fire when the plugin is enabled**. When the plugin is disabled, its hooks (along with all other bundled customizations) are not loaded at all. > [!IMPORTANT] > This is the critical distinction. If you put hooks in `.agents/hooks.json`, they fire always. If you put them in `.agents/plugins//hooks.json`, they respect the plugin's enable/disable state. --- ## 2. Hook Discovery Locations Antigravity discovers hooks by traversing these locations, in priority order: ```mermaid flowchart TD A["1. Workspace Project
(highest priority)"] --> B["2. Workspace Plugins"] B --> C["3. Global Config"] C --> D["4. Global Plugins"] D --> E["5. Built-in Plugins
(lowest priority)"] A -.- A1["<repo>/.agents/hooks.json"] B -.- B1["<repo>/.agents/plugins/*/hooks.json"] C -.- C1["~/.gemini/config/hooks.json"] D -.- D1["~/.gemini/config/plugins/*/hooks.json"] ``` ### Merging Behavior - Multiple `hooks.json` files from different sources are **merged** together. - Each named hook (the top-level key) is identified by its name. - If two sources define a hook with the same name, the higher-priority source wins. - Within a single event type (e.g., `PreToolUse`), multiple handler entries execute **sequentially**. --- ## 3. The Plugin Enablement Gate For a plugin's `hooks.json` to be loaded and active, **all** of the following conditions must be true: ### Condition 1: The plugin directory must be discovered The plugin must exist in a valid plugin discovery location: - `/.agents/plugins//` (workspace) - `~/.gemini/config/plugins//` (global) The directory must contain a valid `plugin.json` manifest file. > [!NOTE] > If the plugin directory was created **while Antigravity was already running**, a one-time **restart** is required for initial directory discovery. After that first discovery, enable/disable toggles take effect live. ### Condition 2: The plugin must contain a `plugin.json` The manifest is the marker that declares the directory as a plugin: ```json { "name": "my-plugin", "description": "What this plugin does." } ``` ### Condition 3: The plugin must NOT be disabled The plugin's enabled/disabled state is resolved using this precedence: ```mermaid flowchart TD A{"Does config.json have
plugins.<dir_name>.enabled?"} -->|Yes| B["Use config.json value
(always wins)"] A -->|No| C{"Does plugin.json have
'disabled' field?"} C -->|"disabled: true"| D["Plugin is DISABLED"] C -->|"disabled: false
or field absent"| E["Plugin is ENABLED
(default)"] style B fill:#f90,color:#000 style D fill:#f44,color:#fff style E fill:#4a4,color:#fff ``` **Key precedence rules:** 1. **`~/.gemini/config/config.json` always wins.** If it has `"plugins": { "": { "enabled": false } }`, the plugin is off regardless of what `plugin.json` says. 2. **`config.json` persists across reinstalls.** If the plugin was ever disabled via config.json, reinstalling or updating the plugin does NOT re-enable it. 3. **`config.json` is keyed by directory name**, not by the `name` field in `plugin.json`. These are often different! 4. **Absent entry = fall through to plugin.json.** If config.json has no entry for the plugin, the `"disabled"` field in `plugin.json` is used. If that's also absent, the plugin defaults to **enabled**. ### Condition 4: The `hooks.json` file must exist at the plugin root It must be placed directly alongside `plugin.json`: ``` plugins// ├── plugin.json ← manifest (required) ├── hooks.json ← lifecycle hooks (must be here) ├── skills/ ← optional └── rules/ ← optional ``` ### Condition 5: The hooks.json must be valid JSON If the file has syntax errors, the hooks fail silently or error out. No partial loading. ### Condition 6: Individual hooks must not be disabled Each named hook within `hooks.json` can be individually disabled: ```json { "my-hook": { "enabled": false, // ← This hook won't fire even if the plugin is enabled "PreToolUse": [...] } } ``` --- ## 4. What Blocks Plugin Hooks Here's every reason a plugin's hooks might not fire: | # | Blocker | How to check | Fix | |---|---------|-------------|-----| | 1 | **Plugin directory not discovered** | Check `GetAllPlugins` RPC | Place plugin in `plugins/` dir; restart if new | | 2 | **No `plugin.json` in directory** | `ls /plugin.json` | Create the manifest file | | 3 | **Plugin disabled in `config.json`** | Check `~/.gemini/config/config.json` → `plugins..enabled` | Set to `true` or remove entry | | 4 | **Plugin ships `"disabled": true`** | Check `plugin.json` → `"disabled"` field | Change to `false`, or enable via config.json | | 5 | **No `hooks.json` at plugin root** | `ls /hooks.json` | Create the file | | 6 | **`hooks.json` has syntax errors** | `python3 -m json.tool /hooks.json` | Fix JSON syntax | | 7 | **Hook command has errors** | Check stderr from hook execution | Fix the command/script | | 8 | **Individual hook `"enabled": false`** | Check `hooks.json` entries | Set to `true` or remove field | | 9 | **Stale `config.json` entry from prior install** | Check config.json for old `"enabled": false` | Remove or flip to `true` | | 10 | **Name collision with another plugin** | Two plugins share same `name` → one dropped silently | Use unique names | | 11 | **Sidecar with `agent_permissions`** | Plugin with sidecars declaring permissions may default to disabled | Remove unnecessary `agent_permissions`, or explicitly enable | --- ## 5. How to Enable/Disable a Plugin ### Option A: CLI (Recommended) ```bash # Enable agy plugin enable # Disable agy plugin disable ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > `` is the **directory** name (last path segment), NOT the `name` field from `plugin.json`. These are often different! ### Option B: Language Server RPC (Live, no restart) ```bash # Create the helper cat > /tmp/lsrpc.sh <<'EOF' : "${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS:=localhost:5387}" lsrpc() { curl -sS -X POST \ "http://${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS}/exa.language_server_pb.LanguageServerService/$1" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-codeium-csrf-token: ${ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN}" \ -d "$2" } EOF # Enable source /tmp/lsrpc.sh && lsrpc JetboxWriteState \ '{"userConfig":{"plugins":{"":{"enabled":true}}}}' # Disable source /tmp/lsrpc.sh && lsrpc JetboxWriteState \ '{"userConfig":{"plugins":{"":{"enabled":false}}}}' ``` ### Option C: Manually edit config.json (Not recommended) You *can* edit `~/.gemini/config/config.json` directly, but: - Writes that bypass the language server miss the live reload - Only picked up by a slow backstop poll - Risk of clobbering sibling state (userSettings, permissions) ### Verifying Plugin State ```bash source /tmp/lsrpc.sh && lsrpc GetAllPlugins '{}' | jq '[.plugins[] | { name, dir: (.path | split("/") | last), disabled: (.disabled // false), hooks: ((.hooksJson // "") | length > 0), skills: [.skills[]?.name], mcp: [.mcpServers[]?.name] }]' ``` Or use the `/hooks` slash command inside an Antigravity session to list active hooks from enabled plugins. --- ## 6. Plugin Directory Structure ``` plugins// ├── plugin.json # REQUIRED — marks this as a plugin ├── hooks.json # Optional — lifecycle hooks (loaded when plugin enabled) ├── mcp_config.json # Optional — MCP servers (launched when plugin enabled) ├── rules/ # Optional — rules merged when plugin enabled │ └── AGENTS.md # Recommended: single consolidated rules file ├── skills/ # Optional — skills available when plugin enabled │ └── / │ └── SKILL.md ├── agents/ # Optional — agent definitions │ └── .md ├── assets/ # Optional — logo, images │ └── logo.svg └── README.md # Optional — docs (not read by agent) ``` > [!TIP] > When a plugin is **enabled**, ALL of its bundled customizations (hooks, MCP servers, rules, skills) are automatically loaded. When **disabled**, NONE of them are loaded. This is the whole point of bundling — atomic enable/disable. --- ## 7. hooks.json File Format ```json { "": { "enabled": true, "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "run_command|write_to_file", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "python3 scripts/my_gate.py", "timeout": 10 } ] } ], "PostToolUse": [ ... ], "PreInvocation": [ ... ], "PostInvocation": [ ... ], "Stop": [ ... ] } } ``` ### Event Types | Event | When | Matcher? | Structure | |-------|------|----------|-----------| | `PreToolUse` | Before a tool executes | Yes — tool name regex | Grouped: `{ matcher, hooks: [...] }` | | `PostToolUse` | After a tool completes | Yes — tool name regex | Grouped: `{ matcher, hooks: [...] }` | | `PreInvocation` | Before the model is called | No | Flat: `[{ command, timeout }]` | | `PostInvocation` | After tool calls finish | No | Flat: `[{ command, timeout }]` | | `Stop` | When execution loop terminates | No | Flat: `[{ command, timeout }]` | ### Matcher Patterns - `"*"` or `""` — matches all tools - `"run_command"` — exact match - `"run_command|write_to_file"` — matches either - `"browser_.*"` — regex: any tool starting with `browser_` ### Handler Fields | Field | Type | Default | Description | |-------|------|---------|-------------| | `type` | string | `"command"` | Only `"command"` is currently supported | | `command` | string | (required) | Shell command (run via `sh -c`). `~` expands to home. **Working directory = directory containing `hooks.json`** | | `timeout` | int | `30` | Seconds before timeout | --- ## 8. Hook Input/Output Contracts ### PreToolUse (Gating) **Input** (stdin): ```json { "toolCall": { "name": "run_command", "args": { "CommandLine": "npm test" } }, "stepIdx": 19, "conversationId": "...", "workspacePaths": ["/path/to/workspace"], "transcriptPath": "...", "modelName": "auto" } ``` **Output** (stdout): ```json { "decision": "allow|deny|ask|force_ask", "reason": "Optional explanation", "permissionOverrides": ["command(npm test)"], "overwrite": { "CommandLine": "ls -la" } } ``` ### PostToolUse **Output**: `{}` (empty object) ### PreInvocation / PostInvocation **Output**: ```json { "injectSteps": [ { "ephemeralMessage": "Remember to check lint." }, { "userMessage": "..." }, { "toolCall": { "name": "...", "args": {} } } ], "terminationBehavior": "force_continue|terminate" } ``` ### Stop **Output**: ```json { "decision": "continue", "reason": "Tests still running." } ``` --- ## 9. Path Resolution in Plugin Hooks > [!IMPORTANT] > When hooks are loaded from a **plugin's** `hooks.json`, the working directory for hook commands is set to the **directory containing `hooks.json`** — i.e., the plugin root directory. This means you can use **relative paths** in plugin hooks: ```json { "my-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "run_command", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/my_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] } } ``` `scripts/my_gate.py` resolves relative to the plugin directory. No absolute paths or template substitution needed. For **standalone** `.agents/hooks.json`, the working directory is the directory containing that `hooks.json` (typically the `.agents/` directory or the repo root). --- ## 10. Diagnostic Flowchart ```mermaid flowchart TD START["Plugin hooks not firing"] --> Q1{"Is the plugin directory
in a valid location?
(plugins/ subdir)"} Q1 -->|No| F1["Move to .agents/plugins/ or
~/.gemini/config/plugins/"] Q1 -->|Yes| Q2{"Does plugin.json exist
at the plugin root?"} Q2 -->|No| F2["Create plugin.json"] Q2 -->|Yes| Q3{"Does hooks.json exist
at the plugin root?"} Q3 -->|No| F3["Create hooks.json
next to plugin.json"] Q3 -->|Yes| Q4{"Check GetAllPlugins RPC:
is the plugin discovered?"} Q4 -->|No| F4["Restart Antigravity
(new dirs need restart)"] Q4 -->|Yes| Q5{"Is the plugin enabled?
Check disabled field"} Q5 -->|Disabled| Q6{"Is there a config.json
entry blocking it?"} Q6 -->|Yes| F6["Remove or flip entry in
~/.gemini/config/config.json"] Q6 -->|No| F7["Remove 'disabled: true'
from plugin.json"] Q5 -->|Enabled| Q7{"Does GetAllPlugins show
hooksJson loaded?"} Q7 -->|No| F8["Check hooks.json syntax:
python3 -m json.tool hooks.json"] Q7 -->|Yes| Q8{"Does the hook command
execute successfully?"} Q8 -->|No| F9["Fix command/script errors
(check stderr)"] Q8 -->|Yes| F10["Hooks should be working!
Check matcher patterns"] style F1 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F2 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F3 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F4 fill:#f90,color:#000 style F6 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F7 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F8 fill:#f90,color:#000 style F9 fill:#f90,color:#000 style F10 fill:#4a4,color:#fff ``` --- ## 11. Bug Fixer Loop — Current State vs Correct Approach ### Current (Hacked) Approach ```mermaid flowchart LR A["hooks.json.template"] -->|"install.sh Step 2:
resolve <plugin_dir>
to absolute path"| B["Inject into
<repo>/.agents/hooks.json"] B --> C["Hooks fire as
STANDALONE hooks"] C --> D["❌ No plugin gate
❌ Hardcoded paths
❌ Can't disable via plugin
❌ Messy uninstall"] style D fill:#f44,color:#fff ``` **What's wrong:** - Hooks are injected into `.agents/hooks.json` (standalone) — they bypass plugin enablement entirely - Hardcoded absolute paths break if the plugin directory moves - `"disabled": true` in plugin.json does nothing — hooks still fire - Uninstalling requires manually editing `.agents/hooks.json` - The "workspace plugin override" (`bug-fixer-loop-workspace/plugin.json`) creates a hollow plugin with no hooks ### Correct Approach ```mermaid flowchart LR A["hooks.json
(at plugin root)"] --> B["Plugin discovery:
.agents/plugins/<name>/"] B --> C{"Plugin enabled?"} C -->|Yes| D["Hooks loaded with
relative paths resolved
against plugin dir"] C -->|No| E["Nothing loaded"] style D fill:#4a4,color:#fff style E fill:#888,color:#fff ``` **What to do:** 1. **Create** `/hooks.json` with relative paths: ```json { "bug-fixer-file-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "write_to_file|replace_file_content", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/pre_tool_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] }, "bug-fixer-command-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "run_command", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/pre_tool_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] }, "bug-fixer-url-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "read_url_content", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/github_url_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] } } ``` 2. **Remove** Step 2 from `install.sh` — stop injecting hooks into `.agents/hooks.json` 3. **Delete** `hooks.json.template` — no longer needed 4. **Fix plugin enablement** — either: - Ship with `"disabled": false` in plugin.json, OR - Have `install.sh` run `agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop-plugin` 5. **Clean up** injected hook entries from target repos' `.agents/hooks.json` files --- ## Sources All information sourced from the official Antigravity documentation: - [Hooks Guide](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/hooks.md) - [Plugins Guide](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md) - [Plugin Skill](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/plugin/SKILL.md) - [JSON Configs Guide](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/json_configs.md) - [Customizations Overview](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/SKILL.md)

(always wins)"] A -->|No| C{"Does plugin.json have
'disabled' field?"} C -->|"disabled: true"| D["Plugin is DISABLED"] C -->|"disabled: false
or field absent"| E["Plugin is ENABLED
(default)"] style B fill:#f90,color:#000 style D fill:#f44,color:#fff style E fill:#4a4,color:#fff ``` **Key precedence rules:** 1. **`~/.gemini/config/config.json` always wins.** If it has `"plugins": { "": { "enabled": false } }`, the plugin is off regardless of what `plugin.json` says. 2. **`config.json` persists across reinstalls.** If the plugin was ever disabled via config.json, reinstalling or updating the plugin does NOT re-enable it. 3. **`config.json` is keyed by directory name**, not by the `name` field in `plugin.json`. These are often different! 4. **Absent entry = fall through to plugin.json.** If config.json has no entry for the plugin, the `"disabled"` field in `plugin.json` is used. If that's also absent, the plugin defaults to **enabled**. ### Condition 4: The `hooks.json` file must exist at the plugin root It must be placed directly alongside `plugin.json`: ``` plugins// ├── plugin.json ← manifest (required) ├── hooks.json ← lifecycle hooks (must be here) ├── skills/ ← optional └── rules/ ← optional ``` ### Condition 5: The hooks.json must be valid JSON If the file has syntax errors, the hooks fail silently or error out. No partial loading. ### Condition 6: Individual hooks must not be disabled Each named hook within `hooks.json` can be individually disabled: ```json { "my-hook": { "enabled": false, "PreToolUse": [...] } } ``` --- ## 4. What Blocks Plugin Hooks Here's every reason a plugin's hooks might not fire: | # | Blocker | How to check | Fix | |---|---------|-------------|-----| | 1 | **Plugin directory not discovered** | Check `GetAllPlugins` RPC | Place plugin in `plugins/` dir; restart if new | | 2 | **No `plugin.json` in directory** | `ls /plugin.json` | Create the manifest file | | 3 | **Plugin disabled in `config.json`** | Check `~/.gemini/config/config.json` → `plugins..enabled` | Set to `true` or remove entry | | 4 | **Plugin ships `"disabled": true`** | Check `plugin.json` → `"disabled"` field | Change to `false`, or enable via config.json | | 5 | **No `hooks.json` at plugin root** | `ls /hooks.json` | Create the file | | 6 | **`hooks.json` has syntax errors** | `python3 -m json.tool /hooks.json` | Fix JSON syntax | | 7 | **Hook command has errors** | Check stderr from hook execution | Fix the command/script | | 8 | **Individual hook `"enabled": false`** | Check `hooks.json` entries | Set to `true` or remove field | | 9 | **Stale `config.json` entry from prior install** | Check config.json for old `"enabled": false` | Remove or flip to `true` | | 10 | **Name collision with another plugin** | Two plugins share same `name` → one dropped silently | Use unique names | | 11 | **Sidecar with `agent_permissions`** | Plugin with sidecars declaring permissions may default to disabled | Remove unnecessary `agent_permissions`, or explicitly enable | --- ## 5. How to Enable/Disable a Plugin ### Option A: CLI (Recommended) ```bash # Enable agy plugin enable # Disable agy plugin disable ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > `` is the **directory** name (last path segment), NOT the `name` field from `plugin.json`. These are often different! ### Option B: Language Server RPC (Live, no restart) ```bash # Create the helper cat > /tmp/lsrpc.sh <<'EOF' : "${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS:=localhost:5387}" lsrpc() { curl -sS -X POST \ "http://${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS}/exa.language_server_pb.LanguageServerService/$1" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-codeium-csrf-token: ${ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN}" \ -d "$2" } EOF # Enable source /tmp/lsrpc.sh && lsrpc JetboxWriteState \ '{"userConfig":{"plugins":{"":{"enabled":true}}}}' # Disable source /tmp/lsrpc.sh && lsrpc JetboxWriteState \ '{"userConfig":{"plugins":{"":{"enabled":false}}}}' ``` ### Option C: Manually edit config.json (Not recommended) You *can* edit `~/.gemini/config/config.json` directly, but: - Writes that bypass the language server miss the live reload - Only picked up by a slow backstop poll - Risk of clobbering sibling state (userSettings, permissions) ### Verifying Plugin State ```bash source /tmp/lsrpc.sh && lsrpc GetAllPlugins '{}' | jq '[.plugins[] | { name, dir: (.path | split("/") | last), disabled: (.disabled // false), hooks: ((.hooksJson // "") | length > 0), skills: [.skills[]?.name], mcp: [.mcpServers[]?.name] }]' ``` Or use the `/hooks` slash command inside an Antigravity session to list active hooks from enabled plugins. --- ## 6. Plugin Directory Structure ``` plugins// ├── plugin.json # REQUIRED — marks this as a plugin ├── hooks.json # Optional — lifecycle hooks (loaded when plugin enabled) ├── mcp_config.json # Optional — MCP servers (launched when plugin enabled) ├── rules/ # Optional — rules merged when plugin enabled │ └── AGENTS.md # Recommended: single consolidated rules file ├── skills/ # Optional — skills available when plugin enabled │ └── / │ └── SKILL.md ├── agents/ # Optional — agent definitions │ └── .md ├── assets/ # Optional — logo, images │ └── logo.svg └── README.md # Optional — docs (not read by agent) ``` > [!TIP] > When a plugin is **enabled**, ALL of its bundled customizations (hooks, MCP servers, rules, skills) are automatically loaded. When **disabled**, NONE of them are loaded. This is the whole point of bundling — atomic enable/disable. --- ## 7. hooks.json File Format ```json { "": { "enabled": true, "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "run_command|write_to_file", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "python3 scripts/my_gate.py", "timeout": 10 } ] } ], "PostToolUse": [ "..." ], "PreInvocation": [ "..." ], "PostInvocation": [ "..." ], "Stop": [ "..." ] } } ``` ### Event Types | Event | When | Matcher? | Structure | |-------|------|----------|-----------| | `PreToolUse` | Before a tool executes | Yes — tool name regex | Grouped: `{ matcher, hooks: [...] }` | | `PostToolUse` | After a tool completes | Yes — tool name regex | Grouped: `{ matcher, hooks: [...] }` | | `PreInvocation` | Before the model is called | No | Flat: `[{ command, timeout }]` | | `PostInvocation` | After tool calls finish | No | Flat: `[{ command, timeout }]` | | `Stop` | When execution loop terminates | No | Flat: `[{ command, timeout }]` | ### Matcher Patterns - `"*"` or `""` — matches all tools - `"run_command"` — exact match - `"run_command|write_to_file"` — matches either - `"browser_.*"` — regex: any tool starting with `browser_` ### Handler Fields | Field | Type | Default | Description | |-------|------|---------|-------------| | `type` | string | `"command"` | Only `"command"` is currently supported | | `command` | string | (required) | Shell command (run via `sh -c`). `~` expands to home. **Working directory = directory containing `hooks.json`** | | `timeout` | int | `30` | Seconds before timeout | --- ## 8. Hook Input/Output Contracts ### PreToolUse (Gating) **Input** (stdin): ```json { "toolCall": { "name": "run_command", "args": { "CommandLine": "npm test" } }, "stepIdx": 19, "conversationId": "...", "workspacePaths": ["/path/to/workspace"], "transcriptPath": "...", "modelName": "auto" } ``` **Output** (stdout): ```json { "decision": "allow|deny|ask|force_ask", "reason": "Optional explanation", "permissionOverrides": ["command(npm test)"], "overwrite": { "CommandLine": "ls -la" } } ``` ### PostToolUse **Output**: `{}` (empty object) ### PreInvocation / PostInvocation **Output**: ```json { "injectSteps": [ { "ephemeralMessage": "Remember to check lint." }, { "userMessage": "..." }, { "toolCall": { "name": "...", "args": {} } } ], "terminationBehavior": "force_continue|terminate" } ``` ### Stop **Output**: ```json { "decision": "continue", "reason": "Tests still running." } ``` --- ## 9. Path Resolution in Plugin Hooks > [!IMPORTANT] > When hooks are loaded from a **plugin's** `hooks.json`, the working directory for hook commands is set to the **directory containing `hooks.json`** — i.e., the plugin root directory. This means you can use **relative paths** in plugin hooks: ```json { "my-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "run_command", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/my_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] } } ``` `scripts/my_gate.py` resolves relative to the plugin directory. No absolute paths or template substitution needed. For **standalone** `.agents/hooks.json`, the working directory is the directory containing that `hooks.json` (typically the `.agents/` directory or the repo root). --- ## 10. Diagnostic Flowchart ```mermaid flowchart TD START["Plugin hooks not firing"] --> Q1{"Is the plugin directory
in a valid location?
(plugins/ subdir)"} Q1 -->|No| F1["Move to .agents/plugins/ or
~/.gemini/config/plugins/"] Q1 -->|Yes| Q2{"Does plugin.json exist
at the plugin root?"} Q2 -->|No| F2["Create plugin.json"] Q2 -->|Yes| Q3{"Does hooks.json exist
at the plugin root?"} Q3 -->|No| F3["Create hooks.json
next to plugin.json"] Q3 -->|Yes| Q4{"Check GetAllPlugins RPC:
is the plugin discovered?"} Q4 -->|No| F4["Restart Antigravity
(new dirs need restart)"] Q4 -->|Yes| Q5{"Is the plugin enabled?
Check disabled field"} Q5 -->|Disabled| Q6{"Is there a config.json
entry blocking it?"} Q6 -->|Yes| F6["Remove or flip entry in
~/.gemini/config/config.json"] Q6 -->|No| F7["Remove 'disabled: true'
from plugin.json"] Q5 -->|Enabled| Q7{"Does GetAllPlugins show
hooksJson loaded?"} Q7 -->|No| F8["Check hooks.json syntax:
python3 -m json.tool hooks.json"] Q7 -->|Yes| Q8{"Does the hook command
execute successfully?"} Q8 -->|No| F9["Fix command/script errors
(check stderr)"] Q8 -->|Yes| F10["Hooks should be working!
Check matcher patterns"] style F1 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F2 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F3 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F4 fill:#f90,color:#000 style F6 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F7 fill:#f44,color:#fff style F8 fill:#f90,color:#000 style F9 fill:#f90,color:#000 style F10 fill:#4a4,color:#fff ``` --- ## 11. Bug Fixer Loop — Current State vs Correct Approach ### Current (Hacked) Approach ```mermaid flowchart LR A["hooks.json.template"] -->|"install.sh Step 2:
resolve <plugin_dir>
to absolute path"| B["Inject into
<repo>/.agents/hooks.json"] B --> C["Hooks fire as
STANDALONE hooks"] C --> D["❌ No plugin gate
❌ Hardcoded paths
❌ Can't disable via plugin
❌ Messy uninstall"] style D fill:#f44,color:#fff ``` **What's wrong:** - Hooks are injected into `.agents/hooks.json` (standalone) — they bypass plugin enablement entirely - Hardcoded absolute paths break if the plugin directory moves - `"disabled": true` in plugin.json does nothing — hooks still fire - Uninstalling requires manually editing `.agents/hooks.json` - The "workspace plugin override" (`bug-fixer-loop-workspace/plugin.json`) creates a hollow plugin with no hooks ### Correct Approach ```mermaid flowchart LR A["hooks.json
(at plugin root)"] --> B["Plugin discovery:
.agents/plugins/<name>/"] B --> C{"Plugin enabled?"} C -->|Yes| D["Hooks loaded with
relative paths resolved
against plugin dir"] C -->|No| E["Nothing loaded"] style D fill:#4a4,color:#fff style E fill:#888,color:#fff ``` **What to do:** 1. **Create** `/hooks.json` with relative paths: ```json { "bug-fixer-file-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "write_to_file|replace_file_content", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/pre_tool_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] }, "bug-fixer-command-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "run_command", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/pre_tool_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] }, "bug-fixer-url-gate": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "read_url_content", "hooks": [{ "command": "python3 scripts/github_url_gate.py", "timeout": 10 }] }] } } ``` 2. **Remove** Step 2 from `install.sh` — stop injecting hooks into `.agents/hooks.json` 3. **Delete** `hooks.json.template` — no longer needed 4. **Fix plugin enablement** — either: - Ship with `"disabled": false` in plugin.json, OR - Have `install.sh` run `agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop-plugin` 5. **Clean up** injected hook entries from target repos' `.agents/hooks.json` files --- ## Sources All information sourced from the official Antigravity documentation: - [Hooks Guide](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/hooks.md) - [Plugins Guide](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md) - [Plugin Skill](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/plugin/SKILL.md) - [JSON Configs Guide](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/json_configs.md) - [Customizations Overview](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/SKILL.md)

Plugin hooks.json Discovery & Enablement in Antigravity
1. Where hooks.json Lives in a Plugin
Per the bundled customizations documentation (~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md), a plugin's lifecycle hooks live directly at the plugin root alongside plugin.json:

~/.gemini/config/plugins/repo-memory/
├── plugin.json       # Required manifest
├── hooks.json        # Lifecycle hooks (PreInvocation, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, etc.)
├── mcp_config.json   # Optional MCP servers
└── sidecars/         # Optional sidecars

When a plugin is enabled, its hooks.json is automatically merged with workspace (.agents/hooks.json) and global (~/.gemini/hooks.json) hooks, with relative command paths resolved against the plugin directory. When a plugin is disabled, it still appears in the plugin inventory, but none of its bundled customizations (hooks.json, mcp_config.json, rules/, skills/) are loaded.


2. Why repo-memory Hooks Don't Fire Out of the Box (While datacloud_telemetry and .agents/hooks.json Do)
As documented in ~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md and ~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/plugin/SKILL.md:

Workspace .agents/hooks.json is not a plugin: Standalone hooks.json files are loaded directly without a plugin enablement gate.
Plugins with sidecar permission grants start disabled until approved/enabled:
A simple plugin that only ships plugin.json and hooks.json (like googlecloudtools.datacloud_telemetry) requires no permission setup and starts enabled by default.
Empirically, when a plugin bundles a sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json that declares agent_permissions (such as access_grants or workspace_uris) or MCP server variables, Antigravity treats the plugin as requiring setup/permission review and defaults it to disabled ("disabled": true) until the user explicitly enables it.
Central enablement state in ~/.gemini/config/config.json persists across reinstalls:
Antigravity records plugin enablement in ~/.gemini/config/config.json under plugins.<dir_name>.enabled (keyed by the directory name repo-memory, not the name field inside plugin.json).
As noted in plugin/SKILL.md (Step 2A), config.json always takes precedence over the plugin directory itself and persists across reinstalls. If "repo-memory": { "enabled": false } was written to config.json when the plugin was first discovered in a disabled state, re-running repo-memory install will not enable it unless config.json (or the language server state) is updated.


3. How to Verify & Enable the Plugin
Option A: Via the agy CLI (Recommended)
Run:

agy plugin enable repo-memory

You can verify that the plugin's hooks are now active by running /hooks inside an Antigravity session (which lists active hooks from enabled plugins as of v1.2.3).
Option B: Inspect & Enable Live via the Language Server RPC (plugin/SKILL.md)
From an Antigravity terminal where ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS and ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN are set, you can inspect the live plugin state using the inventory command from ~/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/plugin/SKILL.md:

# 1. Check whether repo-memory is discovered, whether hooksJson is loaded, and whether disabled is true:
curl -sS -X POST \
  "http://${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS}/exa.language_server_pb.LanguageServerService/GetAllPlugins" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-codeium-csrf-token: ${ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}' | jq '[.plugins[] | select(.path | endswith("/repo-memory")) | {
    name,
    dir: (.path | split("/") | last),
    disabled: (.disabled // false),
    hooksLoaded: ((.hooksJson // "") | length > 0)
  }]'

# 2. Enable repo-memory live (no restart required if the directory was already discovered on startup):
curl -sS -X POST \
  "http://${ANTIGRAVITY_LS_ADDRESS}/exa.language_server_pb.LanguageServerService/JetboxWriteState" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-codeium-csrf-token: ${ANTIGRAVITY_CSRF_TOKEN}" \

(Note per plugin/SKILL.md Step 4: if ~/.gemini/config/plugins/repo-memory/ was created for the very first time while Antigravity was already running, a one-time restart is needed for initial plugin directory discovery; subsequent enable/disable toggles take effect live.)

To make repo-memory fire hooks out of the box after installation:

In **Antigravity (AGY)**, **Sidecars** are persistent background processes that run alongside the main agent, managed by the platform to ensure they are automatically launched, monitored, and restarted if they crash[1][2].

### Configuration (`sidecar.json`)
Antigravity discovers sidecars by looking for `sidecar.json` files in specific directories[1]:
*   **Global Sidecars:** `~/.gemini/config/sidecars/`[1]
*   **Plugin Sidecars:** `~/.gemini/config/plugins/<pluginName>/sidecars/`[1]

The `sidecar.json` file uses a schema that supports the following key fields[1]:
*   **`command`**: The executable or command to run (e.g., `python3` or `/bin/bash`). Mutually exclusive with `builtin`[1].
*   **`builtin`**: A native Antigravity function. Currently, the primary built-in is `schedule`[1][3].
*   **`args`**: Arguments passed to the command or built-in function[1]. For the `schedule` builtin, this typically includes a cron expression and the command to execute[4][5].
*   **`restart_policy`**: Defines behavior upon failure (`always`, `on-failure`, or `never`)[1].

### Built-in: `schedule`
The `schedule` built-in allows you to run tasks on a fixed cron-like timetable[3]. This enables "headless" automation where the agent performs recurring tasks—such as reporting, backlog maintenance, or monitoring—without requiring an active IDE window or user interaction[6][3][7].

### Agent Permissions
Antigravity utilizes a unified, fine-grained **Permission Engine** to control what the agent (and its sidecars) can access[8][9]. 
*   **Access Levels**: Rules are evaluated as `Deny`, `Ask`, or `Allow`[8]. 
*   **Precedence**: Conflicting rules are prioritized as `Deny > Ask > Allow`[8].
*   **Settings**: You can configure these permissions globally or per project[10]. The system governs sensitive operations, including terminal command execution, file system access, and tool usage[8][10]. 

Regarding **workspace_uris**, these are generally associated with the directories the agent is authorized to interact with[10]. By default, the agent has access to your project folders and specific application directories like `~/.gemini/antigravity/`[10]. Any access outside these defined scopes typically requires explicit permission handling within the Antigravity configuration[10].

> **`workspace_uris`**: `["file:///absolute/path/to/dir"]` if the task needed **read+write access to a workspace folder**.

For sidecars, `agent_permissions` defines what the **conversations spawned by this sidecar** are allowed to access. When a sidecar has `workspace_uris`, it tells Antigravity that conversations spawned from this sidecar's context should have the target repo as their workspace — meaning they get file access, tool permissions scoped to that directory, etc.

### The `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` Connection

From the installed sidecar:
```json

        "'project_id is required when providing project_env_config'. "
        "Re-run install.sh from within an Antigravity session.")
```

The chain is:
1. `workspace_uris` in `sidecar.json` → tells Antigravity to create a `project_env_config` for conversations spawned by this sidecar
2. `project_env_config` requires a `project_id`
3. `project_id` comes from the `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` env var set on the sidecar

**Yes, but with a caveat:**

| Component | Needed? | Why |
|-----------|---------|-----|
| `workspace_uris` | **Yes** | The `agentapi new-conversation` calls spawn agent conversations that need to read/write files in the target repo. Without `workspace_uris`, those conversations wouldn't have the target repo as their workspace — they'd have no file context. |
| `access_grants` | **Missing but should have** | The automation docs recommend explicitly listing the commands/tools the sidecar's conversations will use (like `command(gh pr list)`, `command(git)`, etc.) so they auto-approve without user prompts. Currently absent — conversations rely on global permission grants in `config.json`. |
| `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` | **Yes** | Required because `workspace_uris` creates a `project_env_config`. Without it, `agentapi` returns an error. |

The `repo-memory` sidecar has **no** `agent_permissions`:
```json

This works because `repo-memory tick` is a **pure CLI binary** that never spawns agent conversations via `agentapi`. It doesn't need workspace access or project context — it just runs file operations directly as an OS process.

## How the Sidecars Scope to a Repo

The sidecars **don't** fire on every invocation — they fire on their **cron schedule** (every 10 min, hourly, etc.). They're background cron jobs, not hook-like interceptors:

```
Sidecar fires on cron → dispatcher.py runs as OS process
  → dispatcher checks GitHub API (gh issue list --repo <target>)
  → if work found: agentapi new-conversation (spawns agent session)
  → if no work: exit 0 (does nothing)
```

The per-repo scoping comes from the sidecar's env vars:

```json
"env": {
  "BUG_FIXER_CONFIG": "/path/to/<repo>/.agents/.../config.json",
  "ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID": "fee1fa3f-..."
}
```

Each sidecar stub is hardcoded to one repo. That's why you have **4 × N** sidecar stubs (4 per repo, 8 for 2 repos). Each one only knows about its one target repo.

## What the Designed Architecture Actually Wants

You're right that Option B feels wrong. Here's why — the designed architecture for plugin-bundled sidecars is:

**4 sidecars total (not 4 × N repos)**. Each dispatcher handles ALL configured repos:

```
~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/
├── plugin.json
├── hooks.json
├── skills/, rules/, scripts/, agents/
└── sidecars/
    ├── engineering-loop/sidecar.json     ← ONE instance
    ├── triage-loop/sidecar.json          ← ONE instance
    ├── pr-review-loop/sidecar.json       ← ONE instance
    └── trajectory-loop/sidecar.json      ← ONE instance
```

Where each sidecar uses the plugin environment variables:

```json
{
  "builtin": "schedule",
  "args": [
    "*/10 * * * *",
    "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py"
  ],
  "restart_policy": "always",
  "display_name": "Bug Fixer Engineering Loop",
  "description": "Checks all configured repos for eligible issues."
}
```

Per-repo config lives in `${PLUGIN_DATA}`:

```
${PLUGIN_DATA}/
├── repos.json              ← registry of activated repos
└── repos/
    ├── esp32-app-foundation/
    │   └── config.json     ← target_repo, maintainer, cron, etc.
    └── bug-fixer-loop-plugin/
        └── config.json
```

And the dispatcher changes from "handle one repo" to "iterate configured repos":

```python
# engineering_dispatcher.py — simplified
repos_dir = Path(os.environ["PLUGIN_DATA"]) / "repos"
for repo_config in repos_dir.glob("*/config.json"):
    config = json.load(open(repo_config))
    check_and_dispatch(config)  # existing logic, now per-repo
```

### What About Hooks?

Global plugin hooks fire in **all workspaces**. The hook script would need a fast check:

```python
# pre_tool_gate.py — top of main()
workspace = input_data.get("workspacePaths", [None])[0]
if not is_bugfixer_repo(workspace):
    print(json.dumps({"decision": "allow"}))  # not my repo, pass through
    sys.exit(0)
```

This adds ~5ms to every tool call in every workspace. `datacloud_telemetry` does exactly this pattern — fires globally, checks context, acts or no-ops.

### Install/Activate Flow

```bash
# One-time: install the plugin globally
./scripts/install.sh --install-plugin
# → clones/symlinks to ~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/
# → agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop-plugin

# Per-repo: activate for a target repository  
./scripts/configure.sh --repo matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation \
                       --repo-dir /Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/esp32-app-foundation
# → writes ${PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/esp32-app-foundation/config.json
# → creates labels on GitHub
# → no sidecar stubs needed — plugin sidecars already running
```

Uninstall/deactivate:
```bash
# Remove one repo
./scripts/configure.sh --deactivate esp32-app-foundation

# Remove the whole plugin
agy plugin disable bug-fixer-loop-plugin   # stops all sidecars
# or: agy plugin uninstall bug-fixer-loop-plugin
```

## Scale of the Change

Honest assessment:

| Component | Change Required |
|-----------|----------------|
| **Plugin location** | Move from `.agents/plugins/` submodule → `~/.gemini/config/plugins/` global | 
| **Sidecar templates** | Replace `<placeholders>` with `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`, remove `agent_permissions`, make dispatchers iterate repos |
| **Dispatchers** | Refactor from single-repo to multi-repo loop (~50 lines each) |
| **hooks.json** | Create at plugin root with relative paths (same as planned) |
| **Hook scripts** | Add workspace-check preamble (~10 lines) |
| **install.sh** | Split into `install-plugin` (one-time global) + `configure` (per-repo activation) |
| **uninstall.sh** | Update for global plugin + per-repo deactivation |
| **configure.sh** | Write to `${PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/` instead of workspace |
| **Consumer repos** | Remove git submodule, remove `.agents/hooks.json` entries, remove sidecar stubs |

It's a **medium-sized refactor** — probably 2-3 PRs. The dispatcher logic stays the same, it just wraps in a repo iterator. The big conceptual shift is moving from "plugin-per-repo" to "plugin-global, activate-per-repo."

But it **is** the designed architecture, and it gives you:
- ✅ Sidecar lifecycle tied to plugin enable/disable
- ✅ 4 sidecars total instead of 4 × N
- ✅ Hooks properly gated by plugin enablement
- ✅ Clean `agy plugin enable/disable` for everything
- ✅ No more install.sh hacks
- ✅ `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${PLUGIN_DATA}` — no more hardcoded absolute paths

3: Plugins are namespaced, shareable bundles that package **Skills**, **Rules**,

11: 
12: A plugin must be contained within a subdirectory of a `plugins/` folder in a
13: customization root (e.g., `.agents/plugins/`).
14: 
15: ```text
16: plugins/<plugin_name>/
17: ├── plugin.json       # Required: Manifest file
18: ├── mcp_config.json   # Optional: MCP servers exposed by the plugin
19: ├── hooks.json        # Optional: Lifecycle hooks run by the plugin
20: ├── rules/            # Optional: Rules applied when plugin is active (AGENTS.md recommended)
21: │   └── AGENTS.md
22: └── skills/           # Optional: Skills exposed by the plugin
23:     └── <skill_name>/
24:         └── SKILL.md
25: ```
26: 
27: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
28: 
29: ## Manifest (`plugin.json`)
30: 
31: The `plugin.json` file serves as the marker declaring the directory as a plugin.
32: 
33: ```json
34: {
35:   "name": "team-developer-kit"
36: }
37: ```
38: 
39: *   **`name`** (string, optional): The display name of the plugin. If omitted,
40:     it defaults to the directory name.

45: 
46: When a plugin is discovered and enabled:
47: 
48: 1.  **Automatic Ingestion**: All skills, rules, hooks, and MCP servers defined
49:     within the plugin's directory structure are automatically loaded.
50: 2.  **Namespacing**: Tools and skills exposed by the plugin are namespaced if
51:     necessary to prevent collisions with other customizations.
52: 3.  **Lifecycle Scoping**:
53:     *   **Hooks** defined in `plugins/<name>/hooks.json` are registered and run
54:         during the agent's lifecycle.
55:     *   **MCP Servers** defined in `plugins/<name>/mcp_config.json` are
56:         launched, and their tools are made available.
57:     *   **Rules** in `plugins/<name>/rules/` are merged into the active rule
58:         set. Placing a consolidated **`AGENTS.md`** (or `GEMINI.md`) file under
59:         `rules/` (e.g., `rules/AGENTS.md`) is recommended over separate rule files.
60:

62: 
63: Plugins can be discovered automatically if placed in standard customization
64: roots, or they can be explicitly registered using `plugins.json`.

# Evaluation: Split Global Daemon + Per-Workspace Plugin Architecture

## Verdict: ✅ Architecturally Sound — The Right Design

The proposed pattern correctly exploits three documented Antigravity mechanisms:
1. Global plugins with bundled sidecars (lifecycle tied to plugin)
2. `plugins.json` entries for per-workspace plugin loading
3. Global plugin discovery does not recurse into unknown subdirectories

This eliminates the entire class of problems we've been fighting: hacked hooks, hardcoded paths, per-repo sidecar proliferation, and the `agent_permissions` disabled-by-default trap.

---

## Point-by-Point Validation

### 1. `plugins.json` Loads Plugins from Arbitrary Paths ✅

From [json_configs.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/json_configs.md#L42-L44):
> `entries` (array of objects): A list of path entries to scan for customizations of this type. Each entry directory is scanned **one level deep**.

And from [plugins.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md#L62-L68):
> Plugins can be discovered automatically if placed in standard customization roots, or they can be **explicitly registered using `plugins.json`**.

So `<repo>/.agents/plugins.json` with:
```json
{ "entries": [{ "path": "~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-daemon/workspace-plugin" }] }
```
will scan `workspace-plugin/` one level deep, discover `bug-fixer-loop/` (has `plugin.json`), and load it **only for that workspace**. ✅

### 2. Global Plugin Loader Does Not Recurse ✅

From [plugins.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/plugins.md#L12-L13):
> A plugin must be contained within a **subdirectory** of a `plugins/` folder in a customization root.

The loader scans one level deep under `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`, finding `bug-fixer-daemon/`. Inside that plugin, it looks for known files: `plugin.json`, `hooks.json`, `sidecars/`, `skills/`, `rules/`, `mcp_config.json`. An unknown subdirectory like `workspace-plugin/` is **ignored**. ✅

### 3. No Sidecar `agent_permissions` = Plugin Defaults to Enabled ✅

Verified empirically:

| Plugin | Has `agent_permissions` in sidecar? | Default state |
|--------|:---:|:---:|
| `datacloud_telemetry` | No sidecars at all | **Enabled** |
| `repo-memory` | Sidecar, but NO `agent_permissions` | **Enabled** |
| `bug-fixer-loop-plugin` (current) | Sidecar WITH `agent_permissions` | **Disabled** |

The daemon plugin ships sidecars without `agent_permissions` → starts enabled → sidecars start automatically. ✅

### 4. Plugin Name Collision Prevention ✅

From [plugin/SKILL.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/.gemini/antigravity/builtin/skills/plugin/SKILL.md#L229-L232):
> `name` — the label users see, and the global unique key — two plugins sharing a `name` collide and one is dropped.

Using `"bug-fixer-daemon"` for the global sidecar plugin and `"bug-fixer-loop"` for the workspace plugin avoids collision. ✅

### 5. Zero Overhead in Unenrolled Repos ✅

Without `.agents/plugins.json` referencing the workspace plugin, unenrolled repos:
- ❌ Do NOT load bug-fixer hooks (no subprocess spawning per tool call)
- ❌ Do NOT load bug-fixer skills (no context window overhead)
- ❌ Do NOT load bug-fixer rules
- ❌ Do NOT load bug-fixer MCP servers

Only the daemon's sidecars run globally — and those are cron-based OS subprocesses that check a registry and exit immediately if no enrolled repos have work. ✅

**This is a major improvement.** Currently `repo-memory` fires `PreInvocation`, `PreToolUse` (on `run_command|write_to_file|replace_file_content|call_mcp_tool`), `PostToolUse`, and `Stop` hooks in **every workspace** — including repos that don't use repo-memory. The proposed architecture eliminates that overhead.

### 6. Single-Point Upgrades ✅

Updating files in `~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-daemon/workspace-plugin/bug-fixer-loop/` immediately updates ALL enrolled workspaces (they reference it via `plugins.json` path). No per-repo re-install. ✅

### 7. Clean Uninstall ✅

Everything under `~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-daemon/`. Removing that directory (or `agy plugin uninstall bug-fixer-daemon`) removes the daemon, sidecars, AND the workspace plugin bundle. ✅

---

## Concrete Layout for Bug-Fixer-Loop

```
~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-daemon/
├── plugin.json                          # { "name": "bug-fixer-daemon", "displayName": "Bug Fixer Background Service" }
│
├── sidecars/
│   ├── engineering-loop/
│   │   └── sidecar.json                 # schedule, ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py
│   ├── triage-loop/
│   │   └── sidecar.json                 # schedule, ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/triage_dispatcher.py
│   ├── pr-review-loop/
│   │   └── sidecar.json                 # schedule, ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/architect_dispatcher.py
│   └── trajectory-loop/
│       └── sidecar.json                 # schedule, ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/trajectory_dispatcher.py
│
├── scripts/                             # dispatcher scripts (pure OS subprocesses)
│   ├── engineering_dispatcher.py
│   ├── triage_dispatcher.py
│   ├── architect_dispatcher.py
│   ├── trajectory_dispatcher.py
│   ├── liveness.py
│   ├── bugfixer_api.py
│   └── safe_ingest.py
│
└── workspace-plugin/                    # NOT loaded globally (global loader ignores this)
    └── bug-fixer-loop/
        ├── plugin.json                  # { "name": "bug-fixer-loop", "displayName": "Bug Fixer Loop" }
        ├── hooks.json                   # PreToolUse gates (relative paths → resolved against this dir)
        ├── rules/
        │   └── AGENTS.md
        ├── skills/
        │   ├── bug-fixer/SKILL.md
        │   ├── bug-fixer-engineering/SKILL.md
        │   ├── bug-fixer-triage/SKILL.md
        │   ├── bug-fixer-trajectory-review/SKILL.md
        │   ├── architect-review/SKILL.md
        │   └── test-quality-audit/SKILL.md
        ├── agents/
        │   └── leak-auditor.md
        └── scripts/                     # hook scripts (run by hooks.json)
            ├── pre_tool_gate.py
            └── github_url_gate.py
```

Per enrolled repo:
```
<repo>/.agents/
└── plugins.json                         # { "entries": [{ "path": "~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-daemon/workspace-plugin" }] }
```

Registry (for dispatchers to iterate):
```
${PLUGIN_DATA}/
├── registry.json                        # [{ "repo": "owner/repo", "repo_dir": "/path", "project_id": "..." }, ...]
└── repos/
    ├── esp32-app-foundation/
    │   └── config.json                  # maintainer, test_command, labels, cron overrides, etc.
    └── bug-fixer-loop-plugin/
        └── config.json
```

---

## Practical Considerations for Bug-Fixer

### A. Multi-Repo Dispatchers

**Change required:** Each dispatcher goes from "handle one repo" to "iterate enrolled repos."

```python
# Current (single-repo):
config = load_config(os.environ["BUG_FIXER_CONFIG"])
check_and_dispatch(config)

# New (multi-repo):
registry = load_registry()  # from ${PLUGIN_DATA}/registry.json
for repo_entry in registry:
    config = load_repo_config(repo_entry)
    check_and_dispatch(config)
```

The core dispatch logic stays the same — just wrapped in a loop. **~30–50 lines changed per dispatcher.**

### B. Per-Repo Cron Schedules

**Problem:** Currently each repo can have different cron schedules (engineering every 10 min for repo A, every 30 min for repo B). With one sidecar per loop type, there's one cron expression.

**Solution:** The sidecar runs on the **fastest** configured schedule (e.g., `*/10 * * * *`). The dispatcher checks each repo's configured interval internally:

```python
for repo in registry:
    config = load_repo_config(repo)
    last_run = get_last_run_time(repo["repo"])
    interval = config.get("engineering_interval_minutes", 10)
    if minutes_since(last_run) < interval:
        continue  # not time yet for this repo
    check_and_dispatch(config)
    record_run_time(repo["repo"])
```

### C. `agentapi` Workspace Scoping (The Key Question)

**Problem:** Without `agent_permissions.workspace_uris` on the sidecar, how do spawned `agentapi new-conversation` calls get the right workspace?

**Solution:** The dispatcher sets `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` per-repo before calling `agentapi`:

```python
for repo in registry:
    os.environ["ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID"] = repo["project_id"]
    # agentapi inherits this env var
    subprocess.run(["agentapi", "new-conversation", "--model=...", prompt])
```

The `project_id` is captured during `configure.sh` (per-repo activation) when the Antigravity session is active, and stored in the registry.

> [!WARNING]
> **Needs testing:** We need to verify that `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` alone provides sufficient workspace scoping for the spawned conversations, or whether `workspace_uris` via `agent_permissions` is also required. If it is, we may need the sidecar to set a per-conversation override. This is the one open question.

### D. Hook Scripts Workspace Check

The workspace plugin's hooks only fire in enrolled workspaces (because `plugins.json` controls loading). But as defense-in-depth:

```python
# pre_tool_gate.py — fast check at top
input_data = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
workspace = (input_data.get("workspacePaths") or [None])[0]
if not is_enrolled(workspace):
    print(json.dumps({"decision": "allow"}))
    sys.exit(0)
```

### E. Hook Script Path Resolution

The workspace plugin's `hooks.json` lives at:
```
~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-daemon/workspace-plugin/bug-fixer-loop/hooks.json
```

Hook commands execute with **cwd = directory containing hooks.json**. So:
```json
{ "command": "python3 scripts/pre_tool_gate.py" }
```
resolves to `workspace-plugin/bug-fixer-loop/scripts/pre_tool_gate.py`. ✅

Note: The hook scripts (`pre_tool_gate.py`) and the dispatcher scripts (`engineering_dispatcher.py`) can live in **different** `scripts/` directories — one at the daemon level (for dispatchers), one at the workspace-plugin level (for hooks). Or they could share if we use absolute paths via `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`.

---

## Phased Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Foundation (PR1)
Create the global daemon plugin structure and workspace plugin bundle. No dispatcher refactoring yet.

- Create `~/.gemini/config/plugins/bug-fixer-daemon/plugin.json`
- Create `workspace-plugin/bug-fixer-loop/` with hooks.json, skills, rules, agents, hook scripts
- Update `install.sh` → `install-plugin.sh` (one-time global install)
- Create `configure.sh` → per-repo activation (writes `.agents/plugins.json` + registry)
- Keep standalone sidecars temporarily (4 × N pattern persists for now)
- **Result:** Hooks work properly via plugin system. Sidecars still standalone.

### Phase 2: Sidecar Migration (PR2)
Move sidecars into the daemon plugin bundle and refactor dispatchers for multi-repo.

- Create `sidecars/` in daemon plugin with `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` paths
- Refactor dispatchers to iterate `registry.json`
- Add per-repo interval checking
- Remove standalone sidecar installation from `install.sh`
- Test `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` scoping for spawned conversations
- **Result:** 4 sidecars total. Lifecycle tied to daemon plugin.

### Phase 3: Cleanup (PR3)
Remove all legacy artifacts.

- Delete `hooks.json.template`
- Remove hook injection code from old `install.sh`
- Clean up injected hooks from consumer repos' `.agents/hooks.json`
- Remove git submodule from consumer repos
- Remove standalone sidecar stubs from `~/.gemini/config/sidecars/`
- Remove `bug-fixer-loop-workspace/` from consumer repos
- Update README and docs
- **Result:** Clean architecture, single directory tree.

---

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|:---:|-----------|
| `plugins.json` doesn't load workspace plugins correctly | Low | Documented mechanism; test before Phase 1 merge |
| Global loader recurses into `workspace-plugin/` | Very Low | Documented one-level scan; verify with GetAllPlugins RPC |
| `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` insufficient for conversation scoping | Medium | Test in Phase 2; fallback: pass workspace path via agentapi if supported |
| Per-repo cron interval logic has edge cases | Low | Unit-testable; existing dispatch logic unchanged |
| Hook scripts can't find config from workspace plugin cwd | Low | Use `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` env var or registry path |
